Formulation

Current presentation relates to acute physical health concerns (cough, sore throat, shortness of breath) contributing to increased health-related anxiety. Family history of lung cancer may exacerbate anxiety around current symptoms. Primary stressor is illness affecting occupational functioning and health worries. No information regarding psychological or psychiatric diagnoses or risk of self-harm recorded. 

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Reassurance about current symptoms; assessment for serious illness; obtain advice and support for self-management; sick note for absence from work
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide reassurance; monitor for warning signs of deterioration; support safe return to work; address health anxiety in context of physical illness
- Actions (Patient): Monitor symptoms; seek further medical attention if symptoms worsen or do not improve within four to five days; follow advice (paracetamol, fluids, rest); use sick note as needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provided reassurance; issued sick note; advised on symptom management; clear safety-net instructions for medical review if no improvement/clinical deterioration

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Natural course of upper respiratory tract infection; symptom monitoring; red flag symptoms; health anxiety addressed through reassurance; advised when and how to seek further care
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased or sudden breathlessness; persistent or worsening cough; new or unexplained symptoms; lack of improvement within one week
- Coping Strategies: Rest, fluids, paracetamol; reassurance; prompt medical attention if red flags occur
